 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The San Francisco 49ers and Washington Commanders meet on "Monday Night Football."
 Washington enters at 1-3-1 after a frustrating 27-27 overtime tie against the New York Giants. The Commanders had a chance to win late but could not convert.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement San Francisco, meanwhile, is 5-0 and coming off a 32-29 victory over the reigning Super Bowl champions, the Seattle Seahawks. Brock Purdy and the 49ers sit atop the NFC West and could become the first team to win six games this season. 
 TV Channel and Live Stream for Commanders vs 49ers
 Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels (5) celebrates touchdown.Amber Searls-Imagn Images
 Time: 8:15 p.m. ET
 Venue: Levi's Stadium, Santa Clara, California
 TV: ESPN and ABC
 Live stream: Fubo, DIRECTV
 Free options: Free trials from Fubo and DIRECTV for eligible new subscribers
 The game will air nationally on ESPN and ABC. NFL fans without cable can use a qualifying Fubo or DIRECTV streaming free trial to watch the broadcast, subject to eligibility and current promotional terms.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement MNF is also available through the ESPN app with an eligible TV-provider login. NFL+ carries live local and prime-time regular-season games on supported mobile devices, but it is a paid subscription.
 Commanders vs 49ers: Players to Watch
 Jayden Daniels leads the Washington offense as the Commanders seek just their second win of the season.  Running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt is out with a groin injury, which could mean more work for veteran backs Austin Ekeler and Rachaad White. Wide receiver Stefon Diggs is available after dealing with a hamstring issue.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement San Francisco will again rely on Purdy under center alongside running back Christian McCaffrey and tight end George Kittle. Wide receiver Mike Evans, who did not practice during the week due to Achilles and rib injuries, has also been cleared to play. 
 Defensive end Nick Bosa (knee, calf) and wide receiver Deebo Samuel Sr. (hamstring) were ruled out in the final injury report.
